data.title: Lymphogranuloma venereum — viva
data.summary: Sexually transmitted infections · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Lymphogranuloma venereum** (Sexually transmitted infections)_

**Q1. What is LGV?**
- Systemic STI of lymphatic tissue caused by invasive Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2 (L2b — proctitis outbreaks in MSM), L3

**Q2. Stages of LGV?**
- Primary (3–30 days): transient painless papule/ulcer/herpetiform lesion, often unnoticed; urethritis/cervicitis
- Secondary (inguinal syndrome, 2–6 weeks): painful unilateral inguinal lymphadenitis (bubo) with periadenitis, multiple sinuses ('watering-can'); groove sign; constitutional symptoms; or anorectal syndrome (proctocolitis)
- Tertiary: chronic lymphoedema (esthiomene of vulva, saxophone penis), rectal strictures, fistulae, lymphorrhoids, perianal condylomas

**Q3. What is the groove sign?**
- Enlarged inguinal and femoral nodes separated by the inguinal (Poupart's) ligament — seen in ~10–20%; highly suggestive of LGV

**Q4. What is esthiomene?**
- Chronic elephantiasis with ulceration of the vulva (and perineum) in late LGV in women (from Greek 'eating away')

**Q5. Bubo of LGV vs chancroid?**
- LGV: initially painful matted nodes, periadenitis, multiple sinuses, groove sign, primary lesion healed
- Chancroid: unilocular suppurative bubo with single opening, painful ulcers still present

**Q6. What is bubonulus?**
- Painful nodule/abscess along the dorsal lymphatic of the penis (lymphangitis) that may rupture

**Q7. Investigations?**
- NAAT/PCR for C. trachomatis with LGV-specific genotyping (most sensitive) from ulcer, rectal swab or bubo aspirate
- Serology (complement fixation ≥1:64, micro-IF), culture (McCoy cells — difficult); Frei test historical
- Screen for HIV, syphilis, hepatitis

**Q8. Differential diagnosis?**
- Chancroid, syphilis, herpes, donovanosis (pseudobubo — subcutaneous granulomas, not true nodes), tuberculous/pyogenic lymphadenitis, lymphoma, cat-scratch disease, filariasis, Crohn disease (anorectal)

**Q9. Treatment?**
- Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily × 21 days (drug of choice); erythromycin 500 mg four times daily × 21 days in pregnancy; azithromycin 1 g weekly × 3 weeks
- NACO black kit (kit 7) for inguinal bubo — doxycycline × 21 days + azithromycin 1 g
- Aspirate fluctuant nodes through healthy skin; surgery for strictures/elephantiasis; treat partners (contacts within 60 days)

## Quick spotter facts
- Unilateral matted inguinal nodes with groove sign — LGV

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Long case — Lymphogranuloma venereum); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.130. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
